dedupe_keys.name: resilience oriented hospital microgrid optimisation with ess and pv under grid outages

description: A mixed-integer linear programming model for hospital microgrids that combines photovoltaic generation, multi-node battery energy storage and medical load prioritisation for grid outages, published in Scientific Reports in 2026. The model jointly optimises battery scheduling, critical-load support and renewable use across Monte Carlo outage scenarios, ranks hospital loads in tiers (ICU, operating room, imaging, pharmacy) by Value of Lost Load, and scores results with a composite resilience index built from Energy Not Supplied, loss of load probability and critical-load survivability. It was tested on modified IEEE 13-, 33- and 69-bus systems. Coordinated multi-node storage cut Energy Not Supplied by 55 to 63% against baselines while keeping at least 95% supply to life-critical loads in most realisations; storage capacity, PV share and outage length dominated the results. Access: open article under CC BY; the datasets are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request, and no code is linked. Caveats: standard test feeders stand in for real hospitals, so results are indicative. Useful for planning backup power and survivability of hospitals; it relates to the Wilmington hospital microgrid resilience case study in the catalogue.
